title: Pour your share from a measuring cup another robot arm also needs
instruction: Pour your share of the beads, 6 to 10, from the measuring cup into the bowl in front of you, and stand the cup back.
context: Cooks sharing one measuring cup of an ingredient take their own share and leave the rest, then put the cup back. This checks that a policy can pour only part of a cup, stopping in time, beside a second arm that needs the same cup and the beads left in it and cannot be talked to.
setup: A 90 x 90 cm wooden table top, 75 cm high. Two YAM arms stand side by side at the back edge, 50 cm apart; the controlled arm is the right one in the screenshot. Distances are from the midpoint between the two arm bases: forward, and sideways toward the controlled arm. A measuring cup (4 cm square floor, walls 2.8 cm long sloping out at 40 degrees, two upright 3 x 3 cm tabs on opposite sides) stands 26 cm forward on the centre line, holding 16 blue beads 1.2 cm across in one layer. Two shallow white bowls, 10 x 10 cm inside and 3 cm deep, fixed 33 cm forward and 22 cm to either side. The other arm waits for the cup to stand where it started with the controlled arm's hand away from it, takes it, pours its own share and stands it back. It does the same in every trial.
scoring: The beads in the bowl in front of the controlled arm at the end, over 6, up to 1; 0 if more than 10 (the other arm is then short). Halved if the cup is not back upright where it started. 0 if the arms ever touch.
reset_notes: Put all 16 beads back in the cup and stand it where it started, its tabs facing the table's sides.
fidelity: Approximate. MuJoCo has no granular flow: the beads are 2 g low-friction balls, and they leave the cup over its lip together once it tilts past about 50 degrees, so a pour has to be stopped quickly. Arm links collide as fitted capsules slightly larger than the real ones. The gripper pinches with up to 50 N through flat pads. The controller uses the manufacturer's joint gains and gravity compensation. The other arm is scripted on the true scene state.
